newsitem.title: USA: CPI Q2 earnings up on Sears Portrait sales.
newsitem.headline: CPI Q2 earnings up on Sears Portrait sales.

text.p: CPI Corp, which reported second quarter earnings of $1.4 million compared with a year-ago loss of $813,000, said gains were driven by higher sales in its Sears Portrait Studios.
CPI said its portrait studios had operating earnings of $6.8 million, up from $3.4 million a year ago. Sales rose to $56.4 million from $51.5 million.
"We are happy to report that the strength in portrait studio performance that began with the post-Easter period continued throughout the second quarter," Alyn Essman, chairman, said in a statement.
The portrait studio division's operating margin rose to 12.1 percent from 6.6 percent due to proportionately lower cost of sales and operating expenses, he added.

CPI has 1,023 Sears Portrait Studios in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada, as well as 154 Prints Plus wall decor stores and 476 Fox Photo Inc photofinishing locations in a joint venture with Eastman Kodak Co.

CPI said its wall decor division had an operating loss of $1.0 million in the second quarter ended July 19, compared with a year-ago loss of $462,000. Wall decor sales were $12.1 million, compared with $12.0 million a year ago.
Essman said the higher operating loss for wall decor reflected a 3.7 percent decline in same-store sales, plus higher employment and occupancy expenses.
Overall sales for the quarter declined to $68.5 million from $105.4 million, which included about $42 million in sales from a photofinishing business.
"Particularly as we move toward the fourth quarter, the year's peak seasonal period, fixed expenses become a declining component relative to the expected increase in sales," Essman said.
